To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the perception of majority group discrimination against disadvantaged skilled immigrants is not associated with protest actions, but the emotional reaction of frustration, resentment and anger in response to that perception is associated with protest actions; (2) the emotional reaction in response to the perceived discrimination is mediated by status insecurity; (3) the emotional reaction to perceived discrimination is also mediated by collective efficacy; (4) collective efficacy is a strong predictor of protest action.
